mappings.applicability_reason: thr-005 describes an on-path attacker between the Chat Notifier (cmp-002) and the Chat Platform API (cmp-004) on data flow df-003, which carries Deployment Events (ast-001) and may include the secret Chat Bot Token (ast-002). This matches req-DATA-001’s applicable conditions that the system transmits confidential or restricted data and that this data crosses a network boundary the system does not control.

thr-005 involves the Chat Bot Token (ast-002), which is a credential the Chat Notifier (cmp-002) uses to authenticate to the Chat Platform API (cmp-004) when posting deployment notifications, as described in team notes (evd-011). This meets req-SECRET-001’s applicable condition that the system holds a credential that authenticates it to an external platform, so the requirement bears on the custody of the token at issue in this threat.

thr-005 concerns an attacker misusing the Chat Bot Token (ast-002) that the Chat Notifier (cmp-002) uses to reach the Chat Platform API (cmp-004) (evd-006, evd-011). req-SECRET-002 would apply if this access is considered access to customer resources on an external platform and if the chat platform offers short-lived or installation-scoped credentials, but the supplied documentation does not establish either fact.

documentation_gaps.title: Transport protection for Chat Notifier → Chat Platform API is undocumented
documentation_gaps.description: The system overview states that the Chat Notifier formats deployment events and posts them to the internal chat channel over the chat platform’s API (evd-006), and team notes state that this uses a bot token (evd-011). Data flow df-003 crosses trust boundary tb-002 and records encryption_in_transit as unknown. The documentation does not state whether this outbound connection uses HTTPS/TLS, where any TLS termination occurs, or how the Chat Platform API’s identity is verified, so it is not possible to determine whether the Chat Bot Token (ast-002) or Deployment Events (ast-001) are protected in transit against an on-path attacker as described in thr-005.
documentation_gaps.importance: Without documentation of transport protections on df-003, the assessment cannot determine whether req-DATA-001 is satisfied for the Chat Notifier’s calls to the Chat Platform API or whether thr-005 is already mitigated by encryption and authentication in transit.
requested_evidence: Architecture or operations documentation describing the protocol and transport protections used for data flow df-003, including whether HTTPS/TLS is used, where termination occurs, and how the Chat Platform API’s server identity is validated.
Any deployment or network configuration descriptions that show how traffic from the Chat Notifier to the Chat Platform API is routed and protected across trust boundary tb-002.

documentation_gaps.title: Storage and lifetime of the Chat Bot Token are undocumented
documentation_gaps.description: Team notes state that chat posting uses a bot token held by the notifier (evd-011), but the supplied documentation does not describe where or how this token is stored (for example, a managed secrets service, environment variable, or CI variable), how access to it is controlled, or whether it is rotated or short-lived. Reviewer question qst-003 records this as not established. As a result, the assessment cannot determine how the credential at issue in thr-005 is custodied or how easily it can be rotated or revoked after compromise.
documentation_gaps.importance: This gap prevents verification of controls relevant to req-SECRET-001 and potentially req-SECRET-002 for the Chat Bot Token (ast-002). For thr-005, it also obscures how easily the system can respond to token interception on the notifier–chat platform path by revoking, rotating, or limiting the lifetime of the token.
requested_evidence: Documentation naming where the Chat Bot Token is stored (for example, a specific managed secrets service, CI secret store, or configuration mechanism) and how access is controlled.
Any documented rotation or expiry policy for the Chat Bot Token, including whether a short-lived or installation-scoped credential mechanism is used and how rotation is performed in practice.
